py-mng-open-no-encoding.description: Opens a text file without specifying the encoding. The actual encoding depends on the operating system, which can corrupt or break text when the same code runs on a different machine.
py-mng-open-no-encoding.good_code:

    text = f.read()

js-postmessage-no-origin.description: Detects window.addEventListener("message", ...) handlers. AI-scaffolded apps that embed OAuth popups, payment widgets, or third-party iframes use postMessage but frequently omit event.origin validation, allowing any window to send arbitrary messages to the handler.
js-postmessage-no-origin.remediation_action: Always validate event.origin at the top of postMessage handlers. Maintain an allowlist of trusted origins and return immediately if the message is from an unknown source.

js-no-error-handling-async.description: Detects async functions or await expressions that are not wrapped in try/catch blocks and do not chain .catch(). AI-generated code frequently omits error handling, causing unhandled promise rejections that crash the app silently.
js-no-error-handling-async.remediation_action: Wrap all await calls in try/catch. In the catch block, show user-friendly error feedback (toast, alert) and log the error for debugging. Consider a global error handler for uncaught promise rejections.

js-nested-ternary.description: Stacking ternaries (a ? b : c ? d : e or a ? (b ? c : d) : e) collapses what is really a multi-branch decision into a one-liner that is hard to read at a glance.
js-nested-ternary.remediation_action: Refactor the nested ternary into an if/else chain or a small lookup map.

js-function-in-loop.description: Defining a function (arrow, expression, or declaration) inside a for/while loop allocates a fresh function object on each iteration. Over large iteration counts this thrashes the GC and inflates heap usage.
js-function-in-loop.remediation_action: Move the function definition outside the loop and pass loop-scoped values as arguments.

js-fetch-no-timeout.description: Detects fetch() calls and Supabase client operations that do not use an AbortController, timeout, or signal parameter. AI-scaffolded-generated network calls have no timeout — if Supabase is slow or unreachable, the request hangs indefinitely and the UI freezes with a loading spinner.
js-fetch-no-timeout.remediation_action: Use AbortController with a timeout for all network requests. Create a utility function that wraps fetch/Supabase calls with a configurable timeout (e.g., 10 seconds). Show a timeout error message to the user when the deadline is exceeded.
js-fetch-no-timeout.bad_code:
// Hangs forever if Supabase is slow
const { data } = await supabase
  .from('large_table')
  .select('*')
  .order('created_at', { ascending: false })

node-no-lint-config.description: Detects package.json files without ESLint, Biome, or oxlint in devDependencies and no "lint" script defined. AI-scaffolded apps have no code quality tooling — the AI generates code but never validates it against any linting rules.
node-no-lint-config.remediation_action: Install ESLint with typescript-eslint and eslint-plugin-react-hooks (critical for detecting hook rule violations). Alternatively, use Biome for a faster, all-in-one solution. Add a "lint" script to package.json and run it in CI.
